pairs.question: Quis ascendit in caelum et accepit eam et deduxit eam de nubibus? Quis transfretavit mare et invenit illam et adtulit illam super aurum electum?
pairs.answer: Sed qui scit universa novit eam et invenit eam prudentia sua qui praeparavit terram in aeterno tempore et replevit eam pecudibus et quadrupedibus.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question about who has obtained/found wisdom (eam = prudentia/sapientia). Question is the two contiguous interrogative verses 3.29-30. The answer skips the non-answering preamble of 3.31 ('non est qui possit scire viam eius neque qui exquirat semitas eius', a deflection asserting no one can know her way) and begins at the operative answering sentence 3.32 'sed qui scit universa novit eam et invenit eam...'. Answer ends at the first full stop (after 'quadrupedibus'); what follows (3.33 'qui emittit lumen...') continues elaborating God's works rather than answering. Capitalization of first words and terminal punctuation normalized; no Latin altered.
